title: Console Lite Pathway: scope trim, fallback behavior, and acceptance criteria for dashboards/tracing/costs
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Summary: This ticket finalizes a constrained feature set for the Console Lite MVP focused on three areas: dashboard cards, lightweight tracing, and per-route cost breakdowns. The goal is to deliver a usable developer experience within the current engineering capacity and telemetry budget while preserving clear fallback behavior for missing/trimmed features. The PRD had a broader scope (streaming tiles, arbitrary timeframe exports, unlimited trace span depth). After alignment with Eng and Design, we are cutting the higher-risk items and defining acceptance criteria for the trimmed scope.

Goals:
- Ship a compact set of insight cards (4 tile types) with aggregated, non-streaming data.
- Provide a tracing UI limited to recent request traces with max span depth 5 and 30s capture window.
- Provide per-route cost breakdowns at a daily granularity with simple export (CSV single-route) only.

Non-goals (explicit cuts):
- No streaming/real-time tile updates in the Lite launch.
- No multi-route bulk export or scheduled exports.
- No deep trace exploration (>5 span depth) or flamegraph visualizations.
- No long-term retention beyond 30 days for Lite telemetry (enterprise addons remain out of scope).
scope_changes: Remove streaming updates for dashboard tiles — tiles will be refresh-on-demand with 5m cache TTL.
Limit dashboard tile types to: Request QPS, Median Latency, Error Rate, Token Cost per Route (4 tiles).
Tracing: capture and display up to 50 recent traces per route in the last 30s, max span depth 5. Longer traces will be truncated with clear UI messaging.
Cost breakdown: provide daily aggregated per-route cost and token counts; exports limited to single-route CSV for the selected date range (max 14 days).
Defer: alerting rules, trace sampling configuration UI, export scheduling, and multi-tenant retention policies to Dedicated/Private roadmap.
decisions: Adopt cache-first tile model to control telemetry and compute costs — Engineering recommended 5-minute TTL based on load tests.
Tracing truncation chosen over full capture to preserve SLOs for the hosted runtime; UI will show a 'trace truncated' badge if truncated.
Single-route CSV export chosen to minimize backend work and complexity for MVP; product will include a clear note in the UI about export limits.
Acceptance criteria will require UX sign-off on messaging for trimmed features to mitigate support noise.
acceptance_criteria: Four dashboard tiles render for a route and show consistent values in the web console for 95% of requests under test load (see performance test plan).
Tiles update on manual refresh and respect 5m cache TTL; no streaming websocket traffic for tile updates in Lite release.
Tracing: UI shows up to 50 recent traces for a route; traces deeper than 5 spans display a 'truncated' indicator and keep top-level timing correct.
Cost breakdown: per-route daily aggregations must match billing data within 2% for standard workloads over a 7-day baseline window.
CSV export: user can export a single route's daily cost/token numbers for up to 14 days; file includes metadata header with export limits noted.
Design review: UX copy for truncated traces and export limits approved by Design and PM before feature flag flip.
Operational: rollout gated by monitoring alerts showing no more than 3% increase in telemetry ingestion cost in staging and <=1% increase in production after a canary period.
Documentation: Console Help article and QuickStart updated with trimmed capabilities prior to public release.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: enable to 5% of accounts in staging -> run smoke tests for 48h -> increase to 25% in a canary wave for 72h.
If telemetry costs rise >3% in canary, rollback flag and capture dumps for postmortem.
Post-launch: collect qualitative feedback from 10 early users via Solutions Eng; add any high-friction items to backlog for Phase 1.1.
Communications: note trimmed scope in release notes and in onboarding banner inside Console Lite to set expectations.
metrics_and_gates: Telemetry ingestion delta (staging): <= +3% during canary window (5% accounts).
UI latency: dashboard median request render < 300ms for 90th percentile in canary cohort.
Export success rate: CSV generation success >= 98% in canary cohort.
Customer support volume: baseline for related tickets must not exceed 1.5x normal in first 2 weeks; PM to evaluate escalations.

Design (Mateo): ensure 'truncated' state has accessible tooltip and keyboard focusable help link per accessibility guidelines.
SRE (Ben): add synthetic canary job to exercise CSV export path to avoid surprises in production.
Support (Jin): add pre-written support KB entry and templated responses for customers asking about missing export features.
